questions: This applicant carries zero debits on every table, but several cardiac markers sit close to the preferred thresholds at the same time: untreated diastolic 86 (systolic 124), A1c 6.0 with no diabetes diagnosis, total cholesterol 215, age 53. Does the house treat this pattern as a 'combination of cardiac risk factors' under section 16, and if it does, what is done with it - debits added, the best available preferred class capped, or nothing beyond the tables?

Her only miss against the Preferred criteria is diastolic 86 against the 84 ceiling, with systolic 124 well inside and every other Preferred criterion met. Does the house have any practice for a preferred-class blood pressure criterion missed on one component by a small margin - a tolerance, averaging, or a repeat reading - or is the ceiling applied strictly as written so that she lands at Standard Plus?
